html:
Cleopatra VII was the last ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, queen from 51 to 30 BCE, whose alliances with two Roman leaders ended in Rome taking Egypt. She was born in 69 BCE into the Greek-speaking Macedonian dynasty that had ruled Egypt since Alexander's death.

She was well educated, spoke several languages, and is said to have been the only one of her dynasty to learn Egyptian. She came to the throne with her younger brother, who soon drove her out.

Rome by then held the real power in the Mediterranean. When Julius Caesar arrived in Egypt in 48 BCE, Cleopatra won his support. Caesar defeated her brother, who drowned in the fighting, and put her back on the throne. She had a son, Caesarion, whom she said was Caesar's. She was in Rome when Caesar was murdered in 44 BCE.

She then allied with Mark Antony, who controlled the Roman east, and had three children with him. Antony gave her and her children lands in the east, which his rival Octavian, the future Augustus, used to turn Rome against them.

  • In 31 BCE Octavian beat their fleet at the Battle of Actium in Greece.
  • In 30 BCE he took Alexandria. Antony killed himself, and Cleopatra did the same soon after; the story says by the bite of an asp.

Rome made Egypt a province, and Octavian had Caesarion killed. Most of what we know of her comes from Roman writers hostile to her, who painted her as a seductress. Later art and plays, from Shakespeare to Hollywood, built on that image.
